newsitem.title: ALBANIA: SOCCER-ALBANIA UNREST WIPES OUT SOCCER MATCHES.
newsitem.headline: SOCCER-ALBANIA UNREST WIPES OUT SOCCER MATCHES.

text.p: Unrest in Albania sparked by the collapse of pyramid investment schemes has led to cancellation of a friendly soccer international against Macedonia and league matches for the third consecutive week.

"Because of the situation we are sticking with the previous announcement and no matches are to be held this week," Eduard Dervishi, Secretary General of Albania's soccer federation, said by telephone.

He said soccer authorities in Macedonia, a former Yugoslav republic east of Albania, had refused to come to Tirana for Wednesday's match. His federation had turned down a proposal to play in the Macedonian town of Ohrid, just over the border.
"It would not be in our interest to play there," he said.
Albania's right-wing government cancelled all sports events when demonstrators made penniless by the collapse of the schemes set fire to public buildings in several cities.
Mass arrests halted the protests for a week but tens of thousands of impoverished investors have marched through the port of Vlore for the past three days.
"The match cancellations are becoming a problem as the teams have almost stopped training and it has put them in psychological uncertainty," Dervishi said. "But the championship should resume soon."

Dervishi said he hoped Albania's World Cup group nine home qualifiers against Ukraine on March 29 and Germany on April 2 would be unaffected. "We shall formally let UEFA and FIFA know to prevent problems arising," he said.
Albania were suspended by FIFA for a time last year after the Balkan country's sports ministryremoved Dervishi and dissolved the federation's executive committee.

Former Argentine international Mario Kempes, meanwhile, denied press reports he had asked Diego Maradona and Argentina manager Daniel Passarella to help support Lushnje, the troubled Albanian first division side he coaches.
"This was printed in (an Argentine) newspaper, but I have not spoken with Maradona or any other player," Kempes told the Albanian service of Voice of America radio.

Argentine World Cup winner Kempes signed a two-year contract worth $350,000 with first division club Lushnje, sponsored by Pellumb Xhaferri, the detained chief manager of one of five collapsed pyramid schemes.

Brazilians Carlos Eduardo Castro de Souza and Valdemir Souza dos Santos snapped up by Lushnje, Albania's first soccer club to buy foreign players, have left the country following the unrest, while Nigeria's Leonardo Ineh Nosa is still there.
